scope_stage_instruction: Scoping only. Broad discovery query strings should focus on definition, classification, included/excluded segments, adjacent markets, data hierarchy, metric scope, methodology terms, and boundary risks. Do not write confirmed market size, growth rate, market share, channel ranking, competitive landscape, valuation multiples, M&A conclusions, or page-ready claims. Any numerical or directional finding encountered during broad discovery must be stored only as an unvalidated lead.

llm_definition_draft.purpose: LLM-only pre-search draft based on the user brief and general domain understanding. Do not include numbers, market conclusions, rankings, valuation, or investment claims.
llm_definition_draft.working_market_draft: Core category in the user-defined geography with matching customer and distribution logic.
llm_definition_draft.parent_market_draft: Related sector family that includes adjacent product clusters.
llm_definition_draft.broader_market_draft: Industry-adjacent consumer services and supply-chain categories with partial overlap.
included_segments_draft: Primary target category aligned to the user brief
Segments with direct competitive comparison logic
excluded_segments_draft: Unrelated categories outside the target customer set
Purely upstream raw-material businesses without downstream commercialization continuity
adjacent_markets_draft: Support services with shared distribution and buyer access
Cross-category alternatives that can reframe buyer alternatives
ambiguous_boundaries_to_check: Whether adjacent branded consumer products should stay excluded or be included for diligence context
Whether multi-country revenue definitions can be merged for direct comparison
scoping_search_queries: industry definition classification included segments and adjacent categories
industry taxonomy methodology and metric scope by geography

scope_summary.working_market: Working market scope for this engagement as defined by user-provided material.
scope_summary.parent_market: Immediate parent category above the target sector.
scope_summary.broader_market: Related consumer and service clusters with partial overlap.
adjacent_markets: Indirect comparison pools for diligence triangulation

broad: Customer-facing peers with high substitution risk
Channels with similar conversion and retention mechanics
core: Directly comparable peers in the defined sector
Primary business-model segment in user scope
adjacent: Peripheral product/service lines with secondary similarity
Potential white-space peers from adjacent end-user cohorts
excluded: Non-relevant regional variants outside geography definition

included_segments: Directly comparable revenue and geographic segments
Core customer cohort with similar unit economics
Wider peer segments to cross-check scope validity
Related service channels that shape competitive intensity

ambiguous_boundaries.item: Whether adjacent platform models belong in core scope
ambiguous_boundaries.why_ambiguous: These players share channels but differ in business model depth.
ambiguous_boundaries.research_treatment: Treat as scoped-out unless validated by formal research with explicit scope notes.

scope_confidence_rationale: Confidence is provisional until formal boundary and source quality are validated.

can_be_compared_with: global growth context with clear geography mapping
cannot_be_compared_with: private internal figures without methodology disclosure

can_be_compared_with: cross-country comparable releases with aligned definitions
formal research rows backed by reviewed sources

unvalidated_leads.lead: Potential channel-adjacent overlap may inflate peer set if not scoped first.
unvalidated_leads.source_hint: Formal search required for source-backed boundary setting.

required_reconciliations.why_it_matters: Inconsistent scope assumptions can invalidate subsequent evidence mapping.
required_reconciliations.formal_research_requirement: Formal_research_scope_search must confirm final inclusion/exclusion rules.

reconciliation_policy: Validate all scope ambiguities with formal research and record final boundary rules in scope_summary and scope_classification.
formal_research_seed_questions: Which geography and channel constraints define the final metric denominator?
Which segments remain comparable for investor-style peer calibration?
Which user-provided materials are in-scope for direct evidence, and which are context-only?
